questions.subject: English Language
questions.question: Not only the senators but also the clerk of the chamber _______ summoned before the constitutional panel last week.
questions.explanation: Correlative conjunctions 'not only... but also' follow proximity concord. The noun phrase closest to the verb is 'the clerk of the chamber' (singular), and 'last week' requires the past singular verb 'was'.
questions.explanation_short: 'Not only... but also' takes singular past 'was' to match 'the clerk'.
questions.explanation_pidgin: 'Not only... but also' dey follow proximity rule too. 'The clerk' na one person and 'last week' na past tense, so 'was' correct.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in italics: The tribunal decried the *egregious* falsification of electoral returns.
questions.explanation: 'Egregious' means outstandingly bad, shocking, or flagrant.
questions.explanation_pidgin: 'Egregious' mean say the bad thing bad reach extreme level wey shock everybody — 'shockingly bad'.
